_comment: Stonewashed and straight-leg are the two words doing the period work; without them a model returns a modern slim jean every time. REWORDED 2026-09-05: the shirt is worn OPEN OVER A T-SHIRT rather than 'sleeves rolled to the elbow, tucked into' the jeans. Tucked-in-with-a-belt is the detail that made this read as a man's outfit -- the garment was never gendered, the way of wearing it was -- and open over a tee is both plainer and closer to how everybody actually wore a flannel shirt in 2003. The neutral role this preset used to hold passed to tshirt-jeans, which is the default now; this one is the same idea with one more layer.
label: Checked shirt and jeans
wardrobe: a checked flannel shirt worn open over a plain t-shirt, with stonewashed straight-leg jeans
